Metadata.title: Vay Đúng — Choose the right loan, or decide not to borrow
Metadata.description: See the real cost of a loan from licensed lenders, and know when not to borrow.

Home.title: Vay Đúng
Home.tagline: Vay Đúng shows the real cost of a loan, helps you check a lender, and tells you when not to borrow.

points.cost: Works out the real yearly cost, including mandatory fees with a known amount, so you can compare loans.
points.licensed: Compares only products from institutions on the State Bank of Vietnam's list, with the source and the date checked.
points.honest: Tells you plainly when an amount goes over the guideline for what you can repay, and suggests other options.
points.independent: Takes no money from lenders, doesn't sell your information, and doesn't lend.

Home.privacy: No login. Calculations run only on your device.

no_income.title: We don't recommend borrowing without a regular income
no_income.body: A loan has to be repaid every month, even before you find work. Paying late adds more interest and can damage your credit history.

Alternatives.title: What you could do instead
Alternatives.smaller: Borrow less: about {amount} over {term} months could fit (estimate at {lender}'s highest rate).
Alternatives.longer: Repay over a longer time: the monthly payment falls, but the total cost rises.
Alternatives.payDebt: Pay down your current debts before borrowing more.
Alternatives.save: Save part of it first, then borrow less or not at all.
Alternatives.family: Ask family, or ask your employer about a salary advance.
Alternatives.avoid: Don't turn to loan sharks or loan apps of unknown origin. If you're asked to transfer money before receiving a loan, stop and check with the lender's official hotline.
Alternatives.familyNoIncome: Ask family whether they can help for now.

Guidance.title: What to know for this need
Guidance.phone: Buying electronics: ask about installments at the store first. If a plan is advertised as 0%, ask whether any fees or insurance come with it. If none do, it can be cheaper than a cash loan. Compare the total you'd pay.
Guidance.motorbike: Buying a motorbike: compare dealer installments with a cash loan. Some installment loans use the bike as security or set conditions on its registration papers, so ask before signing. The total you'd pay is the number to compare.
Guidance.education: Tuition: first ask about scholarships and paying in stages. If you're a student in difficult circumstances, ask your school or the Vietnam Bank for Social Policies about its student loan programme and whether you qualify.
Guidance.medical: An emergency: check your health insurance and ask family first. If you still need to borrow, use only a licensed lender, even in a hurry.
Guidance.debt: Borrowing to pay debt: be careful, debts can snowball. First ask your current lender about more time or a new repayment schedule. Only take a new loan if its real cost is clearly lower than the old one.
Guidance.living: Borrowing for everyday spending: the loan raises your monthly payments while your income stays the same. See whether you can cut spending or get a salary advance first.
Guidance.other: A cash loan is flexible but can be expensive. Borrow only what you need, and compare the total you'd pay across the options below.
Guidance.urgent: In a hurry: people who need money fast are easier to scam. Be wary if anyone makes you transfer money first, especially to a personal account, before approving or paying out a loan. A genuine fee or insurance charge must be written in the contract. Call the lender's official hotline before transferring anything.

Results.why1: We order by Vay Đúng's estimated real rate, at the highest level the lender publishes, because nobody knows yet which rate you'd get. It includes mandatory fees with a known amount, but not insurance that is optional or may not be required. This order isn't advice on which lender to choose.
Results.why2: A product whose fees are all unknown can't be first, because its real cost may be higher than we can calculate.
Results.why3: No lender pays to be ranked higher. Vay Đúng takes no commission and doesn't sell your information.

Safety.title: Check a lender
Safety.intro: Enter a lender, app or website. We compare it with the State Bank of Vietnam's lists and help you spot signs worth checking.
Safety.privacy: The check runs on your device. We don't send or keep what you enter.
Safety.nameHint: For example: a company name, app name or web address. Don't know the name? Just choose the signs below.
Safety.signsLabel: Have they done any of these?
Safety.signsHint: Optional. Choose whatever applies to you.
Safety.errorEmpty: Please enter a name or choose at least one sign.
Safety.asOf: According to the State Bank of Vietnam's list, as of {date}.
Safety.seeOnList: See the State Bank of Vietnam's list

licensed.title: This name matches an institution on the State Bank of Vietnam's list
licensed.websiteMatch: The address you entered matches this lender's website in our data.
licensed.caution: Compare the full name above with the name in the contract. This result is only about the name: it doesn't mean whoever is contacting you really is this institution, or that the loan is safe or right for you. Scammers can impersonate real lenders, so find the official website or hotline yourself to check.

similar.title: This name resembles one on the list, but doesn't match
similar.body: "{name}" doesn't match any name in our data. You may have mistyped it, it may be an unrelated organisation, or someone may be using a similar name. We're drawing no conclusion about it. Did you mean:
similar.advice: Don't rely on links or phone numbers they send you. Find that lender's official website or hotline yourself and ask.

notFound.title: We didn't find this name in the data we took from the State Bank of Vietnam (as of {date})
notFound.body: We couldn't verify this name. That doesn't mean they're unlicensed or a scam: an app may have a different name from the lending company, and our data doesn't cover every type of institution (see the note below).
notFound.advice: Ask for the company's full name as written in the contract, then check again. If they won't say or have no company name, don't transfer money or send documents.

flag.generic_name: This name contains a general lending phrase, so it isn't enough to tell which company is lending. Ask for the lender's full name.
flag.too_easy: This name uses wording about easy or fast loans. It's something to check, not a conclusion.

stop.title: Stop before you transfer money or send information
stop.body: You chose signs that appear in warnings about loan scams. We can't conclude this is a scam, but don't transfer money or send more information until you've checked, even if they use a real lender's name.

Safety.signsIntro: These are signs to check, taken from warnings reported in the press.

sign.pay_first: Made me make a transfer first (file fee, insurance fee, disbursement fee, deposit…) before I'd get the loan
sign.unlock_fee: Said my file or account number was wrong, then wanted more money to fix or "unlock" it
sign.prove_finance: Made me transfer money to "prove my finances"
sign.otp: Asked for my OTP code, password or PIN
sign.personal_account: Made me transfer money to a person's personal account
sign.contacts: The app won't lend unless I allow access to my contacts, photo library or social media accounts
sign.harassment: Threatened me, or called and messaged my family or colleagues about a debt
sign.hold_id: Wanted personal photos or a relative's phone number as security for the loan
sign.short_term: Lends only for days or a few weeks, and I get less than the approved amount
sign.chat_only: Only contacts me through Zalo or Facebook, or sent a strange link to install an app
sign.no_company: No clear company name, address or contract template

why.pay_first: Hanoi police warn that being told to pay a fee before you get the loan may be a scam. Some licensed lenders do collect insurance at disbursement, so ask the official hotline before transferring anything. Don't rely on a contract sent by message, because contracts can be forged too.
why.unlock_fee: After the first fee, they often give a new reason to ask for more, then disappear.
why.prove_finance: This is one of the ways of asking for money named in warnings about fake loan apps.
why.otp: With your OTP or password, someone else can take money from your account. Don't give it to anyone.
why.personal_account: Money sent to a stranger's personal account may be hard to get back. Ask the lender's official hotline.
why.contacts: Police warn that some apps may take your relatives' numbers to pressure you if you pay late.
why.harassment: Police warn that loan sharks often collect debts this way. This sign alone doesn't show who is doing it, so keep the evidence.
why.hold_id: Hanoi police advise against putting personal information and photos on websites. Don't give these to anyone you can't verify.
why.short_term: When fees are taken as you receive the money and the term is very short, the real cost can be far higher than the approved amount suggests. Ask how much you'll receive, how much you'll repay, and when.
why.chat_only: Scammers can set up fake accounts and pages. Find the official channel yourself, and install apps only from official stores.
why.no_company: If you don't know which company is lending, you can't check its licence.

todo.title: What you should do
todo.official: Find the lender's official website or hotline yourself. Don't use links or phone numbers in messages they send, and don't click ads in search results.
todo.noPayment: Before transferring anything, ask the official hotline whether the payment is genuine.
todo.noOtp: Don't give your OTP, password or PIN to anyone.
todo.apps: Install apps only from the App Store or Google Play, and check the developer's name. Being in these stores doesn't prove an app is genuine.

paid.title: If you've transferred money and suspect a scam
paid.stop: Stop contact. Don't send more money to "get your money back".
paid.evidence: Keep the messages, transfer receipts, app name and screenshots.
paid.police: Take this evidence to your nearest police station to report it.

harassment.title: If you're being threatened over a debt
harassment.body: Stay calm and save messages and screenshots. If your phone can record, record your own calls as evidence. Ask your family to save what they receive too. Report it to your nearest police station.

Safety.disclaimer: This is information for reference, not a legal conclusion about any company, and it doesn't tell you whether a loan is safe. Our data covers only commercial banks, joint-venture banks, wholly foreign-owned banks and finance companies, taken from the State Bank of Vietnam's lists as of {date}; things may have changed since then. We haven't included foreign bank branches, the Vietnam Bank for Social Policies, the Co-operative Bank, leasing companies, microfinance institutions or people's credit funds. Brand names and websites were checked by us and don't come from the list.

who.title: Who runs this site
who.body: Vay Đúng is run by {name}. Contact: {email}.

device.title: What you enter in the questionnaire and lender check
device.body: Your income, debts, age, the amount you need, lender names and the signs you choose are processed only on your device. We don't send them anywhere or store them on a server, and there's no login.
device.language: If you switch language midway through the questionnaire, your answers are kept in this browser for up to 2 minutes so you don't have to retype them, then deleted.

analytics.title: Visit statistics
analytics.body: We use Vercel Web Analytics to see how many people view each page and complete each step of the questionnaire. It doesn't use cookies. It records the page viewed, the site you came from, your estimated city or country, and your device type, operating system and browser, as aggregate statistics. This data is processed outside Vietnam. It receives nothing you enter.

hosting.title: Website hosting
hosting.body: The site is hosted on Vercel, a service outside Vietnam. Like any web server, its servers may log IP addresses and technical request details to run and protect the service.

waitlist.title: News list
waitlist.off: The news list isn't open yet, so we aren't collecting emails right now.
waitlist.on: If you sign up, we keep only your email, when you consented, the version of the consent text and the page's language, to tell you when Vay Đúng officially launches. We delete your email after {months} months at most, or sooner once we've told you.
waitlist.processor: Emails are stored at Supabase in its Singapore region, which is outside Vietnam.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You can ask to see, correct or delete your data, or withdraw your consent, by emailing {email}.

never.title: What we don't do
never.body: We don't sell your data, don't pass your information to lenders, and don't take money for rankings.
